## What you should be able to do tonight

- Deliver any of the week's answers on demand within its time limit.
- Name the one habit that most damages your answers and say what you are doing about it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>50 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Finish anything outstanding from days 344 to 349, then run a random-order set: someone or something picks five of the week's questions at random and you answer each within its limit, cold. Cold and out of order is the condition that matters.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Name the habit: it will be one of starting general before answering, over-qualifying, or going silent when stuck. Write down the specific replacement behaviour rather than an intention to do better.
:::
:::

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Timed mixed set, eleventh sitting: five problems in fifteen minutes. Score and plot all eleven.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> A full mock round, first attempt: fifteen minutes of mixed probability, market making and a behavioural question, in one sitting, with no breaks between them. The transitions are what is being practised.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Estimation under adversarial follow-up: give a Fermi estimate, then defend it when told it is wrong by a factor of ten. The correct response identifies which assumption would have to be wrong, rather than revising the answer.
:::
:::
